pr_title: Remove the additional goroutine and dependency on time in the time budget implementation
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind cleanup
/sig api-machinery

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The factory method `newTimeBudget` now takes a `clock` and uses that
clock for all time related operations.

The `takeAvailable` method now calculates the available budget by
looking at the time elapsed since the last time the method was called.

The instances where the time budget logic is called are also updated
since the implementation does not require a channel to denote stopping
signals anymore.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #95875 

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

Signed-off-by: Nabarun Pal <pal.nabarun95@gmail.com>

issue_context.title: timeBudget shouldn't depend on the real clock
issue_context.body:
Instead of relying on the clock:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/time_budget.go#L60

 we should do something similar to the golang rate-limitter is doing:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/golang.org/x/time/rate/rate.go#L306-L331

Hi, I would like to help on this.
@wojtek-t, can you please provide more context or some guidance on how to proceed?

Sorry for delayed response.

@obeyda - what we should do is to basically:
- instead of having an additional go-routine that every 1s refreshes the budget
- change it roughly to:
(a) keep the value of budget and the last time when we were refreshing it
(b) on takeAvailable method:
  - first recompute takeAvailable, which will be "min(current budget + time elapsed since last refresh * refreshValue, maxAllowedBudget)
 - update last refresh time to now
 - return that value

[We also would need to update the existing tests to match the new logic.]

@obeyda - would you be willing to work on it?

>  One question I had was should the takeAvailable method rely on time.Now() or the current time should be passed on by the caller like in the following:

Let's may be start with:
- passing `clock.Clock` on budget creation to it
- relying on `clock.Now()`

@wojtek-t -- thank you for the thoughts. I drafted a rough implementation in #96707 which still depends on `time`. I will make the change as you suggested and rely solely on a `clock.Clock` instance passed on initialization. I have to rethink the testing strategy a bit, possibly using a `clock.FakeClock`.
Yes - FakeClock is the way to test this.

review_comments: That doesn't work - if we are calling takeAvailable more often than once per second, this will always be zero and we will never refresh anything...
Yes. You're right. Periodic refreshes within a second of interval shouldn't reset the ~accumulated budget and~ `lastRefreshTime`.

So, here is what I am thinking:

```
if `elapsedSeconds` is less than 1,
     don't reset the last refresh time
else
     reset the last refresh time to now
```

The accumulated budget will be returned in both cases.
I added a test scenario for this specific case as well.

It still doesn't work.

If I will be calling that every 1.99s, I will always be adding <time budget>.
So effectively, during 199s, I will add 101*<time budget> instead of 199*<time budget>

This can be mitigated, but I would really like this to be done in more continuous way, given we already touch this code.
